title: Compute f_5(n): triangles in graphs with chromatic number ≥ 5

problemStatement.formal: f_r(n) = \min\{ m : \forall G \text{ on } n \text{ vertices}, \chi(G) \ge r \wedge e(G) \ge m \Rightarrow G \supseteq K_3 \}. \text{ Determine } f_5(n).
problemStatement.plain: f_r(n) is the least number of edges forcing a triangle in an n-vertex graph of chromatic number ≥ r. The cases r=2 (Turán), r=3 (Erdős–Gallai), r=4 (Ren–Wang–Wang–Yang 2024) are known; OQ-03 asks for the first open case f_5(n).
whyMatters: Next frontier after f_4(n) was settled in 2024
Tests the conjectured vertex-shift pattern ⌊(n - C(r-1,2))²/4⌋ at r=5 (predicted shift 6)

proven: f is antitone in r: r ≤ r' ⟹ f r' n ≤ f r n (this entry, axiom-free)
f_5(n) ≤ f_4(n) = ⌊(n-3)²/4⌋ + 6 for n ≥ 150 (this entry, unconditional upper bound)
open: The additive constant c_5 (pattern 1, 2, 6 for r=2,3,4 has no obvious closed form)
Matching lower bound via an explicit triangle-free χ≥5 construction
knownResults.goal: Determine f_5(n), ideally in the conjectured form ⌊(n-6)²/4⌋ + c_5.

currentState.focus: Proved structural scaffolding (antitonicity + shift pattern); f_5(n) itself remains open.
blockers: Computing χ ≥ 5 in Lean for a lower-bound construction (Grötzsch/Mycielskian) is hard
No closed form yet for the additive constant c_5
currentState.nextAction: Formalize a lower-bound construction to complement f_5 ≤ f_4; investigate the constant pattern 1,2,6.

knowledge.progressSummary: Erdos1011OQ03.lean (0 new axioms) proves f is antitone in the chromatic parameter (f_antitone_in_chromatic), giving the unconditional upper bound f_5(n) ≤ f_4(n), and formalizes the vertex-shift pattern chromaticShift r = C(r-1,2) matching 0,1,3 and predicting 6 for r=5. The f_5 conjecture ⌊(n-6)²/4⌋+c is recorded as a Prop. f_5(n) is not computed.
builtItems: Forces / f_forces / f_le_of_forces — clean interface to the sInf-defined threshold f
insights: Antitonicity is immediate from the sInf definition: χ≥r' ⟹ χ≥r makes the defining set for r a subset of that for r', and sInf reverses inclusion.
Nonemptiness of the defining set uses card_edgeFinset_le_card_choose_two: any m > C(n,2) forces a triangle vacuously.
The leading-term shift n - C(r-1,2) fits all three solved cases exactly (0,1,3 → predicts 6).
The additive constants 1,2,6 are the genuinely unresolved part; likely tied to the edge count of the triangle-free χ=r gadget grafted onto the Turán graph.
mathlibGaps: No direct support for computing chromatic number ≥ 5 of explicit constructions (Mycielskian χ lower bounds).
nextSteps: Explicit triangle-free χ≥5 graph with ~⌊(n-6)²/4⌋ edges for a lower bound
Closed form / interpretation of c_r from the gadget edge count
Aristotle for any isolated numeric inequality
